title: Runtime hotpatch: prefix-hash leak + slab fragmentation causing cross-tenant GPU OOM cascade
creator: Ravi Menon
description: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private reported recurring GPU OOMs over a 36-hour window. Symptoms: node-level slab exhaustion, large growth in kvcache tombstone/prefix entries, and long-tail fragmentation that prevented efficient allocator reuse. This ticket tracks the emergency investigation, a minimal hotpatch to reclaim leaked prefix entries, rollout plan, and follow-up remediation work to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: A regression in the prefix-hash normalization path (introduced in runtime-1.24.0) prevented tombstone compaction for certain session churn patterns. Combined with a cold-start microburst policy in Dedicated pools, this allowed kvcache index growth and slab fragmentation to progress until GPU allocators rejected large arena allocations, causing OOMs and cascading session failures.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a dedicated node pool with workload that performs heavy short-lived session creation + streaming decode (replicates customer churn pattern)
Send bursty requests containing varied prompt prefixes that exercise normalization and empty-tool-calls (simulate tenant A and B alternating)
Observe kvcache index growth via metrics: kvcache.prefix_entries, kvcache.tombstones, slab.free_bytes; trigger OOM when slab.free_bytes < threshold
Locally run stress test harness 'tools/runtime-stress --pattern prefix-churn --gpu' (internal) to shorten repro to ~30min
mitigations: Immediate: deploy hotpatch that forces a tombstone compaction pass on nodes where kvcache.tombstones > 50k
Immediate: increase eviction aggressiveness for prefix entries in Dedicated pools for 2-hour window
Short-term: apply per-tenant kvcache quotas to isolate noisy tenants
Long-term: revert normalization regression and add invariant tests to prevent tombstone regressions
resolution: Hotpatch (PR linked) adds a background compaction sweep and a defensive guard to avoid creating duplicate prefix hashes during normalization. Canary rollout on 5% of Dedicated and Hosted nodes; observed immediate reduction in kvcache.tombstones and stabilization of slab free bytes. No customer-facing regressions from patch. Marking as hotpatch-deployed; follow-ups scheduled for full revert and test coverage.
rollout_plan: Canary deploy to 5% of Dedicated pools (non-critical customers) + 2 Hosted AZs (03-03 morning)
Monitor kvcache.tombstones, slab.free_bytes, and GPU OOM rate for 2 hours
If stable, roll to 25% after 4 hours, then to 100% across Dedicated/Hosted within 24 hours
Private/on-prem: publish patch notes and backport instructions; coordinate with SEs for manual installs
tests: Unit: normalization idempotency tests added (prefix dedupe scenarios)
Integration: stress harness reproducer added to CI with GPU emulation stage
E2E: canary telemetry asserts for kvcache.tombstones reduction and slab.free_bytes recovery
Regression: add fuzzing of prefix normalization in nightly suite
